Worker split into two cadences: drain_interval 30s (queue -> rollup + pending, no I/O, crash safety) and send_interval 3600s hourly POST; pending buffer capped, overflow spooled straight to disk; only CLOSED hours ship, shutdown forces the partial hour. Separate spool files runs vs rollups-. API: migration 005 ai_run_rollups (idempotent OVERWRITE not increment - at-least-once drain would double-count), rollup ingest, POST /settle, GET /provisional, GET /rollups/timeline. settle_costs mirrors budget.settle: provisional rows only, total split across covered rows, never rewrite settled, FOR UPDATE lock, and recomputes affected rollup cost cells. Public key forbidden from rollups+settle (overwrite semantics). vault-inference budget.settle now pushes to API on a daemon thread. Tests: ADK 49, API 23, vault-inference 28, all green. vault-monitor tsc clean; 1 PRE-EXISTING services test failure unrelated.

Summary: Implemented the two HF telemetry decisions that are expensive to retrofit. (1) PRIVACY: Spaces will post their own usage and most Spaces are PUBLIC, making a telemetry emitter an exfiltration path aimed at our own API carrying data from people who never consented. Built app/telemetry.py around a fixed ALLOWLIST rather than a denylist - a denylist fails open the moment a field is added. Never emitted from any surface: prompt/completion text OR ANY HASH of it (hashes still correlate users across records and short prompts brute-force trivially), end-user identifiers (IP, session id, HF username, visitor info), Space file paths/cwd (routinely embed usernames), and anything from the request body. Public surfaces get a narrower list still - no host/project/backend, which describe our internal estate. Flagged that the API MUST re-scrub on ingest because a Space posting key can leak and sender-side filtering trusts an uncontrolled client; recommended a write-only key scoped to kind=space. (2) RETROACTIVE SETTLEMENT: embedding cost is knowable only after a period, so rows are written provisional at 0 USD and corrected by an hourly pass rather than estimated - a guess would be indistinguishable from a real figure. Added cost_state column, provisional_rows(), and settle() which splits one settled total across covered rows to preserve per-project attribution and REFUSES to rewrite an already-settled row so the at-least-once drain cannot double-count. /v1/budget now reports provisional_rows so an incomplete total says so. Also agreed and documented: hourly rollup from the start, HF folds in as a third telemetry sibling to ai_sessions and input. Remaining open question: flush

Summary: Designed HF telemetry for vault-monitor AI section (user confirmed read-only via vaultwares-api, same boundary as existing views) and captured the telemetry substrate. KEY DISCOVERY: the router discloses far more than the response body suggests - header x-inference-provider names the provider that ACTUALLY served the request, so cost is now priced from that provider's real rate instead of assuming the most expensive live one; rows carry priced_exactly to distinguish exact from worst-case. Also captured: provider_ms and queue_ms from x-api-call-start/end/x-api-received, X-Request-ID (dedupe key for idempotent ingest), finish_reason (truncation rate), usage.cached_tokens (cache hit rate). Gateway overhead now derivable as latency_ms minus provider_ms - measured live at 535ms wall clock vs 169ms provider time, so two thirds was not the model. RESOLVED THE OPEN DB QUESTION WITHOUT A NEW DECISION: vaultwares-api already owns telemetry DB writes in two production routers (ai_sessions.py, input.py) with POST /api/telemetry/{domain}/batches + x-api-key ingest and unauthenticated GET reads; HF telemetry should be a third sibling. Spool contract matches agent-ledger/scripts/drain-spool.ps1 exactly - the existing *.jsonl to *.jsonl.sent rename IS the current/historical separation the user asked for, no new mechanism needed. Wrote docs/hf-telemetry-design.md with full KPI catalogue (quota row, usage, quality/waste incl. truncation and reasoning overhead, performance percentiles, local models) grounded in fields actually verified present. Documented as unmeasurable: real HF billing and embedding cost (time-billed). Open question flagged: ZeroGPU/Spaces have no local process to spool from. 22/22 pytest, ruff clean. PR #1 was merged by user; opened PR #3 for the follow-up work.

Demucs now reads FFmpeg f32 audio incrementally in model-sized 7.8-second windows, keeps only a preallocated 16kHz mono output, loads Meta safetensors via meta/assign, uses CUDA autocast, and returns weights to CPU. Noted user can override the PR rule at any time by asking clearly. Clarified vaultwares-api does NOT run AI - HTTP inference servers stay in vault-inference, only telemetry ingest goes to the API. BUGS FOUND AND FIXED: (1) reasoning models (Bonsai, R1) write to reasoning_content and return a valid 200 OK with EMPTY string if starved - Bonsai used 1290 tokens one run and 1682 the next on identical input, so 1500 floor truncated half the time; raised to 3000 and added explicit 422; (2) local fallback fired on a 422 client error and started a multi-GB weights download - now only 5xx and never downloads on demand; (3) budget cap was RACEABLE - check() reads and record() writes only after response, so concurrent paid requests all passed against a stale total; added semaphore holding paid calls to one in flight (free ungated). Bug 3 was found by sending the diff through the gateway to the free Bonsai model and posting the review as a GitHub PR comment - the requested delivery pattern, demonstrated working. Verified RTX 3060/12GB constraint drives 4-bit NF4 as mandatory default (7B bf16 needs ~15GB, does not fit). Stack: torch 2.5.1+cu121, transformers 4.49, bitsandbytes 0.50, Python 3.12 venv via uv. VERIFIED ON GPU: qwen2.5-coder-7b 4-bit = 6.28GB weights, 33.3 tok/s @200 tokens, peak 6.33/12GB - comparable to Ollama, so transformers engine retained over llama.cpp/vLLM. bge-m3 embeddings 1024-dim L2-normalized, EN+FR. FIXED 2 REAL BUGS: (1) deadlock where a disconnected streaming client leaked the engine lock permanently, wedging all later generation - reproduced, then restructured so a worker thread owns the lock with unconditional release plus StoppingCriteria cancellation; (2) dtype= kwarg silently ignored, transformers 4.49 requires torch_dtype. Registry estimate corrected 5.5->6.3GB after measurement. Qwen SWA warning confirmed spurious (use_sliding_window False). 10/10 pytest pass, ruff clean. Also updated GLOBAL torch 2.6.0+cpu -> 2.6.0+cu124 (cu121 caps at 2.5.1; chose cu124 to add CUDA without downgrading global), verified with real GPU matmul. Local dev only - no deploy, no tailnet, no Jira, no git commit, no consumers migrated.

Summary: Closed out live translation experimentation. Defaults already correct for 'revert to no partials': -Partials off and -TranslatePartials off, so 'vw live-subs -TranslateTo fr' gives translated finals only; no code change made. Read the kaelri/qwen3.5-mt model page as requested and found three deviations in our implementation: the model ships its own tuned system prompt which we override, it expects a literal 'Translate to <Language>:' user turn while we send 'Translate:' with a 'Previous line:' prefix, and it documents temperature 0.3 / top_p 0.6 while we run temperature 0. Thinking is already suppressed by an empty think block in the template so our think:false is redundant. Ran an A/B on six cues: native format is more faithful on complete sentences (ours mistranslated 'chart' as 'carte' and invented an imperative), ours is better at leaving fragments truncated rather than fabricating endings, latency a wash at 466ms vs 454ms. Neither dominates so nothing changed; documented in utils/TRANSLATION_NOTES.md along with why qwen3:0.6b was disqualified, why a stricter prompt made fabrication worse, that the apparent 'creative filling' was a partial-vs-final display artifact, that Parakeet cannot translate, and that port 8090 is crispASR/parakeet not an LLM. Saved a memory that the user is a native French speaker.

Summary: Added -TranslatePartials to live-subs. First investigated the reported 'creative filling' (meet me in the... -> rejoins moi sous les arbres): tested the model on truncated fragments and it does NOT complete them - 'meet me in the' -> 'rencontre-moi dans', cut off; given the full 'meet me in the shade' it renders 'dans l'ombre' correctly. So the model had seen the complete FINAL while the screen still showed a truncated PARTIAL; the mismatch was a display artifact, not invention. Also tested a stricter never-complete-never-add prompt and it was WORSE (fabricated 'et puis il n'a pas dit autre chose' for 'and then he just'), so the system prompt is unchanged. Implementation: TranslateWorker gained a single-slot pending partial guarded by a lock plus a partial_done signal. Finals always take priority - partials are only translated when the final queue is empty - and only the newest partial is ever translated since older ones are stale on arrival. A _final_serial counter is captured before translating a partial and rechecked after, so a slow partial can never land on top of a newer finalised caption; a final also clears any pending partial. Connected DirectConnection for the same starved-event-loop reason as finals. Verified: 3 rapid partials produced 1 translation, and a final produced 0 stale partial emissions with pending cleared. Registry updated, live-subs now 22 params.

Root cause: LiveSubsApp was a plain Python class, not a QObject, so connecting worker.partial to its _on_partial method gave Qt no receiver affinity and the slot ran DIRECTLY on the ASR thread. It then called overlay.show_partial(), driving a full relayout (setFixedWidth/setFixedHeight/setFixedSize/move/repaint) from a non-GUI thread, which froze Qt - hence unresponsive tray, no subtitles and no output past 'model ready; listening'. Two fixes: (1) moved PartialGate into AsrWorker where it belongs, on the ASR thread, and split the signal into raw partial (feeds the cue stream, so -Partials never changes what -EmitPort publishes) and gated partial_shown (connected straight to overlay.show_partial, a QObject on the GUI thread, so Qt queues it correctly). Gate reset now happens in _emit_final alongside the emit rather than via a lambda on a foreign thread. (2) Made LiveSubsApp inherit QObject so on_status - which touches QAction.setText and the tray tooltip and had the same defect pre-existing - now queues onto the GUI thread. Verified: affinity harness shows 6/6 deliveries on the GUI thread; audited every worker/translator connection; startup smoke test with --translate-to fr --partials stable survived 25s (timeout exit 124) with model warm in 623ms and no hang.

Summary: Fixed caption churn and mixed-language display in live-subs. Diagnosed the 'mix of default + translation' as NOT Bilingual (which defaults off): the overlay renders [last final] + [current partial], and partials are deliberately never translated, so a translated final sat above an untranslated partial. Same root cause as the self-correcting flicker. Added PartialGate with three policies - off (default, nothing until final; stillest and most accurate), stable (only the leading words two consecutive passes agree on, so text grows monotonically and never rewrites; comparison ignores case and trailing punctuation which churn more than the words), all (previous behaviour). Verified against a realistic revision sequence: all=6 screen updates, stable=4 and correctly withheld 'chart' until it settled as 'charts', off=0. Reworked bilingual presentation per user: TranslateWorker.done signal changed from (text,start,end) to (source,translation,start,end) so joining is no longer done with a newline in the worker; SubtitleOverlay gained a second OutlinedLabel in its own panel (translucent rounded background, distinct colour #8FE3FF, 0.88x font) shown only when bilingual is on, and _relayout now measures both labels. Summary: Fixed the silent translator in live-subs - a Qt threading bug I introduced. TranslateWorker.run() is a blocking drain loop connected to tr_thread.started, so it seizes its thread and the thread's event loop never spins. worker.final.connect(translator.submit) is cross-thread, which Qt resolves to QueuedConnection, delivered via that starved event loop - so submit() was never invoked once and no cue was ever queued. Proved it in isolation with a two-thread harness: QueuedConnection submitted=0/translated=0/delivered=0, DirectConnection submitted=3/translated=3/delivered=3. Fixed with an explicit DirectConnection, which is safe because submit() only touches a queue.Queue and run() drains it on the other side. The harness also exposed a cold-load timeout pushing the FIRST caption onto the google fallback, so run() now pre-warms the model before entering the loop; measured 688ms warm then 381ms for the first real cue on GPU. Added submitted/translated counters and one-shot logs so a silent translator is visible next time. Flipped -TranslateDevice default cpu->gpu per user, now that the Parakeet buffer ceiling keeps ASR at a steady ~2GB; updated help text accordingly. Confirmed ollama /api/ps reports size_vram=1.81GB correctly - vram-watch.ps1 reads that HTTP field, not process names, so it is unaffected by ollama spawning llama-server.exe; it read 0 earlier only because the model was never loaded.

Summary: Root-caused and fixed the live-subs VRAM growth. Not a cache problem primarily - the rolling audio buffer grows without bound. In AsrWorker.run the buffer is only trimmed when a cue is actually emittable: the single-segment branch requires (settled or too_long) AND txt.strip() AND s0 >= last_final_end - 0.05. Empty text over music/applause, or a segment overlapping the previous final, falls through to partial and leaves the buffer untouched, so too_long never forces a trim. Simulated the pathological path: buffer reaches 900s after 15 min and 1200s after 20 min of audio, matching the reported 15-20 min onset exactly; Parakeet re-transcribes the whole buffer every 0.7s and its memory scales with input length, hence multi-GB in seconds once the buffer is minutes long. Fix 1: unconditional ceiling on buf enforced right after the block append, independent of every emit guard - simulation now pins the buffer at 12.0s at all durations. Exposed as -MaxUtterance/--max-utterance (default 12s). Fix 2: transcribe_array (the live path) never synced or emptied the CUDA cache, unlike its sibling transcribe_file which does both; added throttled synchronize+empty_cache every 20 calls, since variable-length inputs fragment the caching allocator. Registry updated via vw-gui writer, live-subs now 20 params.

Summary: Fixed crash and diagnosed the ollama failure in live-subs translation. CRASH: I introduced an init-order bug - the translator QThread was started before _build_menu() created act_status, and TranslateWorker.run() emits status on its first line, so on_status hit AttributeError. Fixed by starting the thread after the menu exists, and hardened on_status with getattr since status arrives from worker threads that can outpace or outlive the menu. OLLAMA: not a crash - VRAM contention. GPU was 11875/12288 MiB used with 239 MiB free (Parakeet held by the live-subs pythonw process plus desktop/browser), so ollama could not keep the 1.95GB model resident and evicted it; every cue then paid a ~10s reload. Fixes: (1) new -TranslateDevice defaulting to cpu - measured 1070ms/cue vs 412ms gpu but 0.00GB VRAM, verified GPU untouched after a run; ASR is the critical path so translation must never evict it. (2) keep_alive 30m so the model stays resident between quiet stretches. (3) temperature 0.2 -> 0, now deterministic, which also fixed a mistranslation seen at 0.2. (4) launcher warns when -TranslateDevice gpu is chosen with <3000 MiB free. Registry updated via vw-gui writer, live-subs now 19 params.

FINDINGS: CrispASR docs are NOT thin - docs/tts.md is 1638 lines cataloguing ~32 TTS engines (its own header says 'fourteen', a doc bug worth reporting upstream). cosyvoice3-tts is Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512: Qwen2-0.5B AR speech-token LM + DiT-CFM 10-step Euler + HiFT at 24kHz, 9 languages + 18 Chinese dialects, ships an 8-voice baked bank (zero_shot + fleurs-{en,de,zh,ja,fr,es,ko}), and supports BOTH baked-bank names and native arbitrary-WAV zero-shot cloning via --voice ref.wav --ref-text (ports speech_tokenizer_v3 + CAMPPlus + matcha mel to ggml, speech tokens byte-exact vs ONNX). ~1.2GB via -m auto. crispasr.exe v0.8.25 is ALREADY BUILT at CrispASR/build/bin - no C++ toolchain work needed. BLOCKER FOUND AND FIXED: crispasr.exe died instantly with exit -1073741515 (0xC0000135 STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND) and zero output on both streams. Diagnosed by writing a PE import-table parser rather than guessing: all direct imports of crispasr.exe/crispasr.dll resolved, but ggml-cuda.dll transitively needs cublas64_13.dll, i.e. CrispASR was built against CUDA 13 while PATH exposed only v12.0. The machine HAS v13.3, but CUDA 13 relocated its DLLs from bin/ to bin/x64/ - so even adding v13.3/bin did not help. Prepending 'C:/Program Files/NVIDIA GPU Computing Toolkit/CUDA/v13.3/bin/x64' makes crispasr.exe run (26390 chars of help). Summary: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 01:40 - Added true stroked text outline to the live-subs overlay so captions stay legible on any background. Replaced the QGraphicsDropShadowEffect with a new OutlinedLabel(QLabel) that paints glyphs via QPainterPath: stroke pass with a round-join/round-cap pen of width 2*outline (so N px sits outside the glyph) then a fill pass. A drop shadow only offsets a blurred copy, so text still washes out against similarly-bright backgrounds; stroking every glyph edge is what burned-in subtitles do. Word wrapping is done in OutlinedLabel with QFontMetrics rather than by QLabel, because paintEvent and heightForWidth must agree on line count - if they disagreed the window would be sized for a different number of lines than it draws. Outline scales with font size (max(2, size/7)): 3px at 20pt, 6px at 40pt. Added --outline / -Outline (default 3, 0 disables) to the py script, Start-LiveSubtitles.ps1 and vw-commands.ps1. VERIFICATION NOTE: my first contrast test was invalid - it rendered the widget over a filled pixmap and got byte-identical pixel counts for white and black backgrounds, which proved the widget was painting its own background rather than compositing. Redone properly: render glyphs to a transparent pixmap, composite over each background, then count luminance extremes. Result over #FFFFFF/#000000/#7F7F7F/#F2C230/#2E6FF2 - ~1306 very-light glyph px and ~1900-2100 very-dark outline px present on every mid-tone, and counts now vary with background as they must. Re-ran the layout regression after swapping the label class: centre stable at cx=768, bottom stable at 735, grows upward 658->622, shrinks back 78->114->78, no clipping. Both ps1 parse clean.

Summary: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 14:31 - v3.7.1 (commit d999201, pushed). ROOT CAUSE of 'only 2 frames, rest black, tab stalled at 2min': abandoning a seek does not cancel it. Both capture loops set video.currentTime, waited for seeked OR a 1500ms timeout, then drew. When seeks exceed 1500ms (remote/HLS/large files) the loop gives up and assigns currentTime again, which SUPERSEDES the still-pending seek - so the element perpetually re-seeks, never settles, the position barely advances (hence a 34-min video stuck near 2min), and nearly every drawImage captures a stale or empty decoder. Occasionally one seek wins the race = the 1-2 good frames. Compounded by seeked firing before the decoder paints. FIX: new src/lib/frame-capture.ts is now the single implementation for BOTH capture sites - waits for each seek to genuinely settle (8s budget), confirms position + readyState, waits for a real paint (requestVideoFrameCallback with double-rAF fallback), then draws; a timed-out seek SKIPS its frame instead of recording a stale one; uniform frames dropped; runs yielding fewer than MIN_USABLE_FRAMES=4 are discarded rather than stored (a thin/black preview looks captured so nothing retried it); per-run counts logged (usable/timedOut/blank/tainted). NOTE: src/scripts/scraper-player.ts had NEVER received the frame-paint fix applied to processor.ts in v3.6.1 - I had only patched the offscreen path - and it had separately been raised to 30 segments which made the stalling worse; both now share the same 10-frame path. 7 new tests including a fake <video> that reproduces the superseded-seek stall and the all-black capture. Verified tsc clean, vitest 41/41, build OK. User will test.

Summary: Sun 03 Aug 2026. DA3-Streaming PHASE 2 COMPLETE for 0.00 USD - pose converter written and VALIDATED. Created vaultwares_studio/streaming_convert.py converting streaming's flat output (camera_poses.txt C2W + intrinsic.txt + combined_pcd.ply) into transforms.json + sparse_pc.ply so Job B/splatfacto needs zero changes. Validation method: ran streaming on EXACTLY the 80 frames the known-good da3-standard run (local-run-20260713-022745) used, then Umeyama-aligned trajectories. Key insight enabling independent tests: the OpenCV->OpenGL flip negates Y/Z rotation columns but leaves the translation column untouched, so POSITION validates C2W-vs-W2C while ORIENTATION validates the flip. RESULTS: orientation median 9.07deg with flip vs 178.91deg without (near-perfect inversion = decisive); position RMSE 11.9pct of extent correct vs 26.0pct if wrongly inverting. Both conventions confirmed: do NOT invert (streaming already emits C2W), DO apply diag(1,-1,-1,1) on the right. 16 tests pin both failure modes; mutation-tested both (removing flip and adding inversion each break the suite). Residual analysed and is TAIL DRIFT not a converter bug: frames 16-63 agree to 5-7deg median, frames 64-79 degrade to 36deg median - accumulated SIM3 drift with loop_enable:False on frames sampled ~1.6s apart (adversarial for a sequential-video method). This raises phase 5 loop closure from optional to likely-required for long sequences. Explicitly NOT an accuracy claim - reference is another DA3 estimate not ground truth; numbers validate conventions only. 128 tests passing. Pushed 966be28 to main with v1.2.0 bump. Phases 1+2 both done at zero cost; phase 3 (full 500 frames -> processed_min.zip) is next and is the real value decision point.

Summary: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 07:55 - v3.7.0 (commit 97ff7f4, pushed). Implemented the two crypto items flagged in the review. (1) ARGON2ID OFF-THREAD: deriveKek returned Promise.resolve(argon2id(...)) with a comment claiming it kept callers off the event loop - it does not, Promise.resolve wraps an already-computed value, so the full ~1.6s derivation stalled the background worker that also serves preview.get/capture/vault messages. crypto-vault now exposes a swappable KdfRunner via setKdfRunner (validates returned key length and passes options through untouched so a runner cannot silently weaken the KDF); src/lib/argon-worker.ts computes it in a Worker, src/lib/argon-kdf-host.ts installs it. IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT: Worker is NOT exposed in Chrome MV3 service workers (only Firefox's event page), so the host probes typeof Worker and falls back to inline derivation - fallback is exactly the previous behaviour. New esbuild step emits dist/argon-worker.js. Argon2 params UNCHANGED (t=3 m=64MiB) - that cost is the only defense for a 4-digit PIN. (2) ENCRYPT WHILE LOCKED: wrapping the per-blob DEK only ever needed the ML-KEM public key, which is already stored in cleartext in VaultMaterial. (3) Three keys in the user's proposed config (input_width, input_height, precision) DO NOT EXIST in base_config.yaml - resolution is set by pre-resizing frames; real defaults are Model.chunk_size=120 / Model.overlap=60 nested under Model:, not 65/22 flat. (4) Proposed 65-chunk @ 672x378 will not fit 24GB: 60 @ 504x378 is already 21.2/24GB, and at patch-14 the proposal is 84,240 tokens vs 58,320 = 1.44x, so linear scaling alone lands ~30GB. Plan starts from benchmarked 60/30 @ 504x378 with upstream's 50pct overlap on a10g-small. Extra deps flagged: faiss-gpu (highest risk, PyPI version unmaintained; loop_enable:False is the phase-1 escape hatch), numba (JIT warmup), pypose. Weights are local file paths not HF IDs, and loop closure needs a separate DINO-SALAD checkpoint we do not fetch at all. Highest-risk piece identified: the pose converter, since streaming emits C2W where existing da3_to_transforms expects w2c and inverts - wrong convention trains cleanly while being wrong, so phase 2 validates trajectory against the known-good da3-standard run before spending on training. Summary: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 20:45 - Diagnosed and fixed the broken preview storage/playback pipeline. Root cause: commit 82e4169 (06 Jun 2026) reverted the preview transport from Array.from(bytes) back to raw Uint8Array over browser.runtime.sendMessage. Runtime messages are JSON-serialized, so a Uint8Array arrives as a numeric-key object and new Uint8Array(obj) rebuilds as 0 bytes - corrupting BOTH preview.save (stored 0-byte records) and preview.get (returned 0-byte blobs). PreviewThumb then silently bailed on blob.size<100, so no preview ever rendered. Fix: base64 transport (blobB64) in vault-client savePreview/getPreview and the background preview.save/preview.get handlers, matching the existing base64 codec used for VaultMaterial. Also: background refuses to store empty payloads; runCapturePipeline no longer clears data.thumbnail before the preview is durably persisted and now falls through to regeneration when the write fails; PreviewThumb treats undersized blobs as a cache miss so retry/regeneration runs. Added src/lib/preview-transport.test.ts (6 tests) covering the wire boundary and round trip. Verified: vitest 13/13 pass, esbuild bundles background+processor clean, vite build clean. NOTE pre-existing blocker: npm run build fails at tsc because the vaultwares-themes submodule ships crypto-vault.js only (no .ts), so vault-runtime.ts type imports do not resolve. dist/ NOT rebuilt - fix is not live in the packaged extension until that is resolved.

Summary: FIXED mini-omni2 S2S runaway generation in CrispASR. Chain of three defects, each verified: (1) MO2_EOA = 4096 sat one past the sampler range - mo2_sample_token was called with MO2_AUDIO_VOCAB = 4096 and loops i < vocab, so index 4096 was unreachable and end-of-audio could never be selected; text was unaffected because MO2_EOT 151936 is inside text_vocab_size 152000, exactly explaining why text stopped at 15 tokens while audio ran to the cap. Added MO2_AUDIO_SAMPLE_VOCAB = MO2_EOA + 1. (2) Naive fix then stopped at step 1, so added a step >= 7 guard - the 7 audio streams are layershifted and stream 6 is most delayed, making early EOA spurious. (3) THE ACTUAL FIX: -n/--max-new-tokens was silently ignored on the S2S path. mo2_generate_dual was called with a hardcoded 2048 at both call sites, and separately crispasr_backend_mini_omni2.cpp declared speech_to_speech(..., const whisper_params& /*params*/) with params explicitly unused, so mini_omni2_set_max_new_tokens was only ever called from transcribe(). Wired the setter into speech_to_speech and replaced both hardcoded 2048s with ctx->max_new_tokens. S2S IS BROKEN. Found and fixed a real defect: MO2_EOA = 4096 sits one past the end of the sampler range (mo2_sample_token called with MO2_AUDIO_VOCAB = 4096 loops i < vocab so only reaches 4095), making end-of-audio unreachable; the text stream is unaffected because MO2_EOT 151936 is inside text_vocab_size 152000, which exactly explains why text stopped at 15 tokens while audio ran to the hardcoded 2048 cap producing 175s of audio. Added MO2_AUDIO_SAMPLE_VOCAB = MO2_EOA + 1 and a step >= 7 delay guard (7 layershifted streams, stream 6 is most delayed so early EOA is spurious). Result improved 2048 steps/175s -> 978 steps/83s with natural termination instead of hitting the cap, but STILL WRONG: a 9-token reply should be 2-3s. Audio analysis proves the surplus is degenerate, not speech - per-second RMS flat at ~0.02 across all 83s with no pauses, and self-similarity cos 0.00-0.07 so it is not looping either, just continuous babble. Conclusion: second defect

Root cause was a 3-year toolchain gap, not a small bug: CUDA 12.0 host_config.h rejects _MSC_VER >= 1940 while VS 2026 ships MSVC 14.51 (_MSC_VER 1951, cl 19.51.36248). Installed CUDA 13.3 via winget (Nvidia.CUDA 13.3) whose host_config.h allows 1920-1959, covering 1951. VERIFIED empirically before building: compiled AND ran a trivial sm_86 kernel against VS 2026 -> 'cuda ok'. Configure now reports: Found CUDAToolkit 13.3.73, CUDA compiler NVIDIA 13.3.73 with host compiler MSVC 19.51.36248.0, CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86, Including CUDA backend, Configuring done. Build progressing through 844 targets compiling .cu objects. Secondary blocker 'No CUDA toolset found' (CUDA MSBuild .props absent from VS 2026, since CUDA 12.0's installer only knew VS 2017-2022) never needed fixing because build-windows.bat configures with -G Ninja, which invokes nvcc directly. Had to move the stale build/ dir aside (43 references to CUDA v12.0 in CMakeCache would have silently reused the old toolkit) -> renamed build.old-cuda12. Also had to pin CUDA_PATH and PATH to v13.3 since nvcc on PATH still resolved to v12.0 and CUDA_PATH was empty. VS 2022 BuildTools (installed earlier at user request) turned out UNNECESSARY - its MSVC 14.44 is _MSC_VER 1944, which CUDA 12.0 also rejects (caps at 1939); left installed as harmless fallback, instance still flagged isComplete=0 so vswhere skips it. Build harness notes: PowerShell Set-Location does not carry into cmd /c, and cmd mangles quoted paths containing spaces ('Github Repos') making build-windows.bat appear 'not recognized'; worked around by importing vcvars64 env into PowerShell and calling cmake directly.

The real cost was precision: L.Fabric(devices=1, strategy='auto') defaults to 32-true so the whole GPT ran in fp32. Set precision via new MINIOMNI_PRECISION env var (default bf16-true) and cast audio_feature to the model dtype at the whisper->GPT boundary, plus mel to whisper's dtype. MEASURED: 4.3GB -> 2.87GB per instance (33% cut, ~2.9GB saved across two instances); output verified IDENTICAL to fp32 (55 chunks, 6.49s vs 6.485s, valid audio, first chunk 0.61s). Whisper fp16 attempted and REVERTED (MINIOMNI_WHISPER_HALF default 0): whisper's custom LayerNorm upcasts activations to fp32 while weights stay fp16 -> 'expected scalar type Float but found Half'. Also noted litgpt expands k/v to all 14 heads before caching (config is GQA with n_query_groups=2), so the cache is 7x larger than the architecture needs - ~288MB/instance available if the expansion is moved after the cache with SDPA enable_gqa (torch 2.8 supports it); NOT applied. vLLM confirmed inapplicable: mini-omni is a custom litgpt multi-codebook model with 8 parallel audio heads, no vLLM implementation exists. Fixed start_duo.bat --max-tokens 500->800 (500 was below the ~504-token encoding of a 10s capture, causing 500 errors); documented that input encodes ~50 tok/s and generation ~18 tok/s of speech. NEXT: user moving to CrispASR + GGUF quantized models, has a CUDA-not-found bug to fix.

Therefore B's audio reaches NO bus and cannot possibly reach A - the 'Speech detected' events in bridge A were A hearing its OWN voice looping back (A -> CABLE Input -> CABLE Output -> Strip0 -> B1 -> A) plus the user's Realtek mic. Additionally Bus[0]/A1 output device is set to CABLE Input, closing a feedback loop A1 -> CABLE Input -> CABLE Output -> Strip0 -> A1. User's headphones sit on B1, which is why they hear their own mic. Required fix (Voicemeeter GUI, not code): Strip2 B1=ON and A1=ON; Strip0 B1=OFF; Strip1 B1=OFF; reassign A1 bus device away from CABLE Input. Awaiting user decision on whether their mic should stay in the conversation.

Summary: Thu 30 Jul 2026. Root-caused the upside-down viewport: NOT a viewer regression and NOT a missing one-time flip fix. compute_alignment() PCAs over all points and picks up-direction via skewness = mean((proj/std)^3), a third moment hypersensitive to outliers. ~1% of DA3 gaussians sat beyond 10x core radius (max 416x), stretching bbox 1.4 -> 581. Measured: raw gives up=[0,+1,0] skew=32.75 flipped=False tilt=nan; keep-95/98/99 all give up=[~0.1,-0.99,~0.1] skew~0.35 flipped=True tilt~9deg. The up vector INVERTS once outliers are removed - that sign flip is the 180. New vaultwares_studio/splat_filter.py: clamp_opacity (DA3 returns +inf logits, 403 in this cloud, nan-poisons gaussian_merge quality scoring) + sanitize_splat (per-axis quantile envelope, axis-aligned not radial since scenes are ~4x wider than tall). Used quantiles not stddev because with 1% of mass at 400x core, sigma is huge and 2-sigma keeps everything - explained this to the user who had suggested 2SD. Wired via convert_splat_outputs keep_quantile, default 1.0 (no filter); only feed-forward presets opt in at 0.95, trained splatfacto unaffected. Verified on real green run: 4503479 -> 4042127 gaussians, extent 646.1 -> 1.6, skewness 32.75 -> 0.30 (trained run is 1.07), viewer default auto-framing now works with no manual camera, scene reads correctly (pergola/brick wall/lawn/path legible where before smeared blobs). Also fixed latent NaN: arccos(abs(dot)) when dot rounds past 1.0. 10 new tests incl. a regression guard reproducing the flip. 112 passing. Reverted vaultwares-themes submodule change per user (using official colors). Pushed d0bea71 to main with v1.1.2 bump. Also confirmed DA3-Streaming's da3_streaming/ dir is NOT pip-installed (pyproject packages=[src/depth_anything_3]) so integration requires vendoring.

Summary: Diagnosed onn 4K black screen via adb logcat. App launched fine (Displayed +2s764ms), no crash, no native error, zero JS console output because WebChromeClient had no onConsoleMessage override. Root cause: Vite emits script type=module, Chromium fetches module scripts with CORS, and from file:///android_asset the origin is opaque so the module is blocked and #root stays empty. Fix: serve bundled UI via WebViewAssetLoader over https://appassets.androidplatform.net, add onConsoleMessage + onReceivedError logging. Found 3 further blockers for the real-config test: network_security_config.xml was never referenced in the manifest (dead config), cleartext blocked to http Comet host, and PlaybackUrlValidator only allowed cleartext to 10.0.2.2/localhost so Comet stream URLs would be silently rejected. Added scoped carve-outs for 100.67.25.118 plus MIXED_CONTENT_ALWAYS_ALLOW. Device ping to Comet host = 100% loss; box not yet on tailnet. Gradle cannot run in this environment so none of the Kotlin is compile-verified.

Summary: FXV + PKT tube site overhaul. FXV: dropped iframe-only providers (freesexvideos, spankbang); rewired provider profiles for owned-player only (mp4/HLS); added eporner as new direct-stream source with detail-page extraction (fxv_extract_eporner_source); added fxv_actor + fxv_studio taxonomies; per-source actor/studio extraction; hardened per-source fetchers to skip candidates without extractable direct mp4/m3u8/webm URLs (topvid now requires HLS manifest extraction inline); fxv_resolve_runtime_embed falls back to 'unsupported' instead of 'iframe'; updated source catalog + domain map + admin allowlist hints. PKT: added pkt_actor + pkt_studio taxonomies; tightened per-source XPath (xvideos requires video_<digits> + non-channel anchor, xhamster requires /videos/ link, spankbang requires /<key>/video/); added URL_REJECT_PATTERNS (channels/playlists/profiles/series) and CONTENT_REJECT_PATTERNS ('Trust and Safety', 'podcast', 'episode', etc.) to fix prior PH-podcast contamination; redtube API handler now extracts actors from stars/models/pornstars + applies same content filters; added handle_wipe_and_backfill admin handler (requires typed WIPE confirmation) that deletes every pkt_video post, clears seen+cursors+poisoned keywords, then runs bulk fetch across xvideos+xhamster+spankbang+redtube targeting ~50 pages each. Shared: rewrote pkt-player.bundle.js to support hls.js via jsdelivr CDN for non-Safari browsers, added 'unsupported' player mode with source-page link CTA, removed automatic iframe fallback on HLS failures; mirrored JS+CSS to both plugins. Templates: reduced FXV archive inline ad (12->24), removed FXV in-player overlay ad, reduced PKT archive inline ad (3->15), removed PKT below-embed ad slot, added actor+studio chip rows to single-video templates. CSS: added .pkt-player-modal__unsupported + credit chip styles; harmonized PKT brand-icon fallback paths and play-icon fallback SVG (removed lone emoji). All modified PHP lints clean.

Summary: Round 3 feedback fixes â€” eight items. (1) CRITICAL bug fix: prompts/textareas were uneditable because FlowCanvas initialized rfNodes from storeNodes once and never re-synced. Added a useEffect in FlowCanvas that propagates store data changes (params, label) to rfNodes while leaving position/measured state untouched (preserves the visibility:hidden fix from earlier sessions). Identity-checks on params and label avoid spurious re-renders. (2) Toast system: new src/ui/components/Toast.tsx with module-level event hub (pushToast/dismissToast from anywhere) and ToastHost mounted at App root; renders top-right stack with auto-dismiss (6s default, 4s for success); three tones (error/success/info) with matching tokens. App.tsx now pushes 'success' on clean run, 'error' on per-node or top-level failure + auto-opens the inspector. (3) Execution errors moved to TOP of NodeParamPanel â€” banner with the failure detail + a Reset button; the old bottom error block was removed. Per-node text/json outputs still render below (image results render inline ON the comfyui_workflow node). (4) Removed the auto-created Display node from loadFromComfyWorkflow; the master flow is now just the single comfyui_workflow node, with results rendering inline (gallery + thumbnails). Eliminates the disconnected 'Result' node that felt orphaned. (5) Inline image result on ComfyUIWorkflowNode: when the workflow succeeds and the result has imageUrl/imageUrls, the gallery renders inside the node card itself; click any thumb opens full-size in a new tab. (6) New InlineSeedInput in canvas/nodes/inline.tsx â€” number input with a dice button (Lucide Dice5) that fills a 31-bit random int. ComfyUIWorkflowNode routes any input key named 'seed' through this control. (7) Size presets dropdown â€” when a workflow exposes both 'width' and 'height' in input_paths, a single 'size' InlineSelect drives both (512Â², 768Â², 1024Â², portrait/landscape variants, Custom reveals manual w/h number inputs). Exported SIZE_PRESETS array from inline.tsx. (8) NodeId pill â€” small mono badge at the bottom of every node card showing 'node#<short-id>'; tooltip on hover reveals the full id. shortenNodeId helper formats numeric/short/UUID ids consistently. (9) Persisted last-used inputs: ComfyUIWorkflowNode reads localStorage['vw:lastInputs:<workflow_id>'] on mount if all inputs are empty, prefills non-image fields (upload tokens excluded â€” they expire); debounced 400ms save on every input change. Each user gets their own browser-local memory of last prompt/seed/size per workflow. Deployed dist (assets/index-BxACQy3N.js).

Summary: Identified and fixed the real cause of the startup crash. After scanning a directory, the frontend called schedule-idle-previews with all items. For large folders or cloud directories (like iCloud Photos with 2,100+ items), this ran over 6,000 synchronous I/O operations (fs.existsSync) in a single loop on the main process thread, blocking the Electron main thread and triggering a native access violation crash/watchdog lock. Optimized the handler in previews.js to skip automatic background previews for cloud-backed directories (iCloud, OneDrive, Dropbox, etc.) and limited active batch size to 80 items in other folders. Rebuilt installer successfully.

Summary: Landed A2: full real-time progress + cancel for comfyui_workflow nodes. Backend (vaultwares-pipelines): added websockets dependency (16.0) to .venv + requirements.txt. _execute_comfyui_graph now takes optional progress_cb + cancel_event args. Spawns _comfyui_ws_listener as an asyncio.Task that subscribes to ws://127.0.0.1:8188/ws?clientId=<id>, filters events by prompt_id, calls progress_cb with executing/progress/executed/execution_error/execution_success/execution_cached events. If cancel_event is set during execution, POSTs to ComfyUI's /interrupt and raises RuntimeError('canceled'). _execute_workflow_run plumbs both through. Job worker creates: (a) a progress_cb closure that maintains a progress_state dict and writes it to job.progress with throttling (~5 Hz), (b) a watch_cancel asyncio.Task that polls the job record once per second and sets cancel_event when status==canceled. JobSummary/JobDetail gained a progress field. New GET /jobs/recent endpoint (registered before /jobs/{job_id} to avoid the same path-conflict the validation endpoint hit) returns the caller's most recently-updated job, filterable by kind and CSV status; admins see all jobs, non-admins only their own (matched via requested_by.username or special 'vault-flows' tag). Frontend (vault-flows): listed JobSummary + JobProgress types in client.ts; getRecentJob(opts) handles the 'null' body case; cancelJob(id) calls POST /jobs/{id}/cancel. New ExecutionProgressOverlay.tsx renders a fixed bottom-right card while executionStatus==='running' â€” polls /jobs/recent at 1 Hz, shows a pulsing accent dot, progress bar (when total>0), current message, node + step counter, elapsed time, and a Cancel button that calls cancelJob. App.tsx mounts the overlay. Verified end-to-end: started a 30-step run, observed live step progress (poll showed step 4/12, then step 2/30 etc, with current node id 3), POST /jobs/{id}/cancel mid-execution â†’ worker tripped /interrupt â†’ /flows/run returned with error='ComfyUI workflow was canceled', final job status=canceled. Deployed dist (assets/index-DCi4ZtfE.js) atomically.

Frontend (src/api/client.ts): setToken/getToken now read/write sessionStorage key 'vw_jwt' with try/catch fallback to in-memory. Added clearToken() for use on stale-token detection. In-memory mirror kept for fetch-path perf. getMe() return type corrected from {id,username,role} to MeResponse{username,is_admin} matching pipelines schema. App.tsx: useEffect on mount that, if getToken() is set, calls getMe() and either rehydrates currentUser (success) or calls clearToken()+nulls user (401). This makes page refresh in the same tab keep the user logged in, while tab close still clears the token. Pipelines (.env): JWT_TTL_SECONDS=3600 â€” verified via login -> JWT payload exp-iat=3600s. NSSM service restarted. Built + deployed dist (assets/index-GzA-V8ki.js) atomically to greencloud-vps; live on flows.vaultwares.ca + noddit.org. Tradeoff acknowledged: sessionStorage tokens are XSS-readable but vault-flows has no untrusted user content injection points; httpOnly cookie auth was considered but requires a bigger pipelines refactor and isn't needed yet.

Summary: Three workflow-toolchain improvements addressing 'workflow runs in ComfyUI but fails validation' false positives. (1) Converter (convert_proven_workflows.py): skips nodes with mode==2 (muted) and mode==4 (bypassed); for bypassed nodes, rewires consumer links from bypassed_node.output[N] to whatever feeds bypassed_node.input[N], following chains of bypasses. This is exactly what ComfyUI's editor's 'Bypass' mode does at runtime. Eliminates dangling links + 'missing model' false positives where the referenced model was in a bypassed node. (2) Fixer (fix_workflows.py): smarter _core_key() that strips quant markers (FP16/FP8/Q2_K/etc), distillation markers (DMD/DMD2/distilled), AIO/base tags, and minor-version suffixes (V1.0/V1.1/v1-1) â€” so different-quant or patch-version files of the same base model are treated as drop-in substitutes. Closest_match() now uses the core-key tier as high-confidence matching (returns first match, prefers top-level files over nested copies). Also added Pass 3: normalize_load_image_widgets() replaces baked-in LoadImage filenames with a placeholder ('000.jpeg' from D:\\comfyui\\resources\\comfyui\\inputs) so ComfyUI's validator passes; the worker overrides at runtime. (3) Diagnostic (dump_workflows_diagnostic.py): validate_locally() now exempts LoadImage's image input from validation for any node referenced by step.image_inputs[] â€” runtime-overridden inputs are never structurally broken from the worker's POV. Re-seeded: 13/13 workflows now match the fixed JSONs (muted nodes dropped, bypasses rewired). New verdict tally: PASS=3 (biglove-photo, ipadapter-faceswap, z-image-turbo-text2img), BLOCKED_SUBGRAPH=4 (custom-realistic, flux-conditioner-sampler-upscaler, qwen-image-text2img, gonzalomo-dmd-v30), BLOCKED_UNKNOWN_PACK=3 (copilot/flux2-klein-faceswap/wan22 â€” AI-invented), BROKEN_WIRING=2 (basic-lora-text2img orphan upscale chain, qwen-edit-multi-angle unwired CLIP), BLOCKED_MISSING_MODEL=1 (openpose-i2i), VALIDATION_OTHER=1 (qwen-image-edit-4step references muted ReferenceLatent). All remaining issues are real workflow content problems requiring editor surgery.

Summary: Big multi-piece update. (1) Signed image URLs: /comfyui-image/{token} + /uploads/image/{token} endpoints in pipelines, both signed with JWT_SECRET, both unauthenticated by design (token IS the credential). _execute_comfyui_graph now mints signed URLs via _sign_comfyui_image_token instead of base64-inflating images as data URIs. New env COMFYUI_URL_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS=3600. (2) Image upload: POST /uploads/image accepts multipart, writes to UPLOADS_DIR with random name, returns signed upload-token. GET /uploads/image/{token} serves it back. _resolve_image_ref_to_path validates tokens, _upload_to_comfyui pushes local file into ComfyUI input folder. Env: UPLOADS_DIR=./_uploads, UPLOADS_MAX_BYTES=20MB, UPLOADS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS=86400. Nginx vhosts (flows.vaultwares.ca + noddit.org) bumped client_max_body_size to 25m. (3) New image_input node type in vault-flows: ImageInputNode.tsx renders file picker + thumbnail, uploads on selection, stores image_ref+preview_url+filename in params. Worker flow runner: image_input nodes emit kind=image with imageUrl=preview_url and output=ref-token so downstream comfyui_workflow nodes can pick it up via {{input}} template. (4) _handle_comfyui_workflow now template-substitutes upstream into string values in params.inputs (so {source_image: '{{input}}'} from an image_input upstream just works). (5) Workflow's comfyui_graph step gets new optional image_inputs: ['key','key',...] list â€” keys whose values are upload-tokens get resolved by the worker before submitting the graph (_resolve_image_inputs decodes the token, posts to ComfyUI /upload/image, substitutes the resulting ComfyUI filename into the LoadImage node). (6) Bulk converter (scripts/convert_proven_workflows.py): walks 13 ComfyUI editor-format workflows in C:/Users/Administrator/ComfyUI/user/default/workflows/Proven_Workflows. Pulls ComfyUI /object_info to drive widget-vs-link conversion (handles control_after_generate sibling widget for seed inputs). Detects API-format pass-through. For unknown custom-node types (Flux2KleinCheckpointLoader, FaceAlign, FaceDetectorInsightFace, ImagePasteFace, WAN2_2_I2V_*, VideoHelperSuite_ImagesToVideo): preserves the node + its links + widget_values as best-effort with a warning so ComfyUI's error is the source of truth. Heuristics extract primary model (CheckpointLoader/UnetLoader inputs), LoRA names, positive/negative prompts (via KSampler positive/negative links to CLIPTextEncode), seed path, and image input slots (LoadImage nodes â†’ source_image/target_image/reference_image keys). NAME_MAP gives each workflow a clean id+display name (e.g. flux2-klein-faceswap, qwen-image-edit-4step, wan22-img2video). Idempotent via PUT-then-POST. 13/13 seeded successfully. Catalog now has 14 workflows (13 from Proven_Workflows + z-image-turbo-text2img). End-to-end verified through https://flows.vaultwares.ca: upload PNG -> image_input node -> biglove-photo comfyui_workflow node -> ComfyUI received the file via /upload/image and ran VAEEncode against it (failed only because bigLove checkpoint lacks a baked-in VAE; the wiring is correct, that's a workflow-content issue).

Summary: Wired the comfyui_workflow node to actually call ComfyUI end-to-end. (1) Replaced placeholder _job_worker in pipelines api_server.py â€” kind=workflow_run jobs now call _execute_workflow_run, which loads the workflow's first comfyui_graph step, applies input_paths substitutions from job payload inputs, and dispatches to _execute_comfyui_graph. (2) _execute_comfyui_graph posts the API-format graph to ComfyUI /prompt with a random client_id, polls /history/{prompt_id} every 1.5s until status.completed or status_str=='error', extracts image refs from outputs[*].images, fetches the first one via /view, base64-encodes it as a data:image/png URI (so the SPA can render via <img src> without a second authenticated request). (3) Added _apply_input_paths helper that deep-copies the graph and walks dotted paths (e.g. '5.inputs.text') to substitute values from the inputs dict before submission. (4) _handle_comfyui_workflow (flow runner) now passes node.params.inputs through to job payload. (5) New env: COMFYUI_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8188, COMFYUI_PROMPT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=300. (6) Seeded workflow 'z-image-turbo-text2img' in pipelines DB via POST /workflows â€” single comfyui_graph step using ckpt z-Image-Turbo-FP8-AIO.safetensors, 6-step KSampler euler/simple CFG 1.0 at 1024x1024, input_paths for prompt/negative_prompt/seed/steps/width/height. (7) End-to-end verified: vault-flows graph with [input -> comfyui_workflow(z-image-turbo-text2img, inputs={prompt,seed}) -> display] returned in 1m 27s (incl. first-call model warmup), produced a real PNG image (2.2 MB data URI, valid PNG signature 89504e470d0a1a0a) of the requested 'glowing crystal cave with bioluminescent mushrooms', saved as vault-flows-zimage_00001_.png in ComfyUI's output dir; display node correctly forwards the upstream image payload (kind='image', imageUrl=data URI). Also restarted Postgres which had stopped between sessions.

Summary: Built the vault-flows graph execution layer. Backend (vaultwares-pipelines/api_server.py): added POST /flows/run that accepts a vault-flows Flow {nodes, edges} and walks it topologically. Per-node behavior: input emits params.value (or prompt/topic/text fallback); llm calls Ollama /api/generate with model/temperature/system/prompt, substituting {{input}}/{{value}}/{{context}} placeholders from upstream output; transform applies a template; display/output pass upstream through. Returns {results: ExecutionResult[]} in execution order; per-node errors don't abort the run, downstream still receives whatever upstream produced. Added GET /flows/models that proxies Ollama /api/tags so the SPA can discover available models + check reachability. New env vars: OLLAMA_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:11434), OLLAMA_DEFAULT_MODEL (llama3), OLLAMA_CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (120). Used httpx (already in venv) for async Ollama calls. Frontend (vault-flows/src/api/client.ts): switched runFlow from POST /workflows/run {flow} (which was the ComfyUI job-queue endpoint) to POST /flows/run {flow} (the new graph runner). Rebuilt and atomically redeployed to /var/www/vault-flows/dist on greencloud-vps (staged dist.new, mv to dist, chown www-data). Verified end-to-end via https://flows.vaultwares.ca: pass-through graph (input -> display) returns correct topological output; LLM node with bogus model returns clean per-node error 'Model X not available in Ollama. Pull it with: ollama pull X'. Ollama on operator box currently has 0 models â€” runner will activate the moment a model is pulled; presets default to model='llama3' so they'll need an update once the user finishes pulling gemma.

Summary: Implemented buffered real-time ESRGAN upscaling pipeline. Architecture: main.js producer processes video in 60-frame chunks (2s@30fps) — ffmpeg extracts raw PNGs, 4 parallel realesrgan-ncnn-vulkan processes using realesr-animevideov3-x2 model, ffmpeg re-encodes upscaled PNGs to fragmented MP4 segments (frag_keyframe+empty_moov), segment buffer sent via IPC webContents.send. Renderer MediaSource consumer: onUpscaleChunk listener appends ArrayBuffer segments via SourceBuffer in sequence mode with serialized queue. LEAD_CHUNKS=3 means 3 chunks are pre-processed ahead. Upscale badge shows live status. Toggle OFF restores original src at same currentTime.

My response: ship Scenario B (product owner / recipe-as-deliverable) first, Scenario A (self-adapting customer product) is destination not MVP; the expert interrogation system is the moat (spec-level questions, no leading questions, standardized catalog); recipe must be compositional/pattern-based not enumerative (named patterns + bindings + overrides + bespoke islands); deliverable is a project not a file (prose + assets + tests + interview transcript); diagnostic side-effect: failure-to-port is itself a signal making vault-port a low-stakes audit tool. Posed Q4 (deliverable layout straw man with intent.md/ux/domain/assets/tests/interview.md/port.yaml), Q5 (beachhead â€” proposed recursive dogfood option of vault-port porting vaultwares-agentciation itself), Q6 (interview format â€” hybrid form+Socratic likely wins, design question is when to drop from form into Socratic). No code yet, design phase ongoing.

(2) Even if COLMAP were installed, the pipeline has NO exporter code after ns-train splatfacto completes â€” it checks if cloud.usda exists and if cloud.ply exists, but neither ns-process-data nor ns-train writes those files. _write_placeholder_ply() and _write_placeholder_reconstruction() always fire. Available: ffmpeg, ffprobe, ns-process-data (system Python312), ns-train (system Python312), open3d, pxr. Missing: colmap binary only. Fix requires: install COLMAP binary, then add gsplat exporter code that copies/converts the trained model PLY output into cloud.ply and writes real USD from point cloud data.
